title: Does The Bible Contradict Science
paragraphs: Exploring the Relationship Between the Bible and Science

The question of whether the Bible contradicts science is one that has engaged Christians, skeptics, and scholars for generations. This study seeks to examine how the Bible and scientific discovery intersect, overlap, or diverge, especially through an Evangelical lens that upholds the authority and inerrancy of Scripture.
The Bible’s Purpose: Spiritual Truths Over Scientific Textbook

The Bible presents itself primarily as God’s revelation for the salvation and spiritual formation of humanity. Its primary aim is not to function as a comprehensive scientific manual, but rather to reveal God’s character, the human need for redemption, and His plan of salvation through Jesus Christ.
All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting and training in righteousness, so that the servant of God may be thoroughly equipped for every good work. -
2 Timothy 3:16-17 NIV
This passage emphasizes the Bible’s authority and sufficiency for spiritual instruction, not for exhaustive scientific explanation.
Creation and the Natural World: Compatible or Contradictory?

Genesis 1-2 provides a theological account of creation, revealing God as the sovereign Creator of all things. Some interpret these chapters as a literal, six-day creation, while others see them as a literary framework or poetic account that communicates profound truths about God and humanity.
In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. -
Genesis 1:1 NIV

Christians hold varying views on how to harmonize these chapters with scientific theories such as the Big Bang or evolution. The key mainstream approach is to affirm that God is the Creator, while allowing room for differing interpretations on the mechanisms He used—so long as these do not compromise the core doctrine that creation was a purposeful act of God.
God’s Order in Nature and Scientific Discovery

The Bible affirms that creation displays order, predictability, and purpose—attributes that make scientific inquiry possible. Far from being at odds, the pursuit of science can be seen as uncovering the intricacies of God’s handiwork.
The heavens declare the glory of God; the skies proclaim the work of his hands. -
Psalm 19:1 NIV

For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities—his eternal power and divine nature—have been clearly seen, being understood from what has been made, so that people are without excuse. -
Romans 1:20 NIV
These verses suggest that the natural world points to God, and understanding it can enhance our appreciation for the Creator.
Science and Scripture: Apparent Contradictions

Apparent contradictions often arise from differing interpretations—either of Scripture or of scientific data. For example, pre-scientific descriptions of the world (such as the “sun rising”) reflect the language and understanding of the original audience, not scientific error.
The sun rises and the sun sets, and hurries back to where it rises. -
Ecclesiastes 1:5 NIV
Such language is phenomenological (describing what is seen), not a scientific assertion about astronomy.
Salvation, Christ, and the Limits of Science

While science has expanded human knowledge about the material world, it cannot answer ultimate questions about purpose, morality, and salvation. The Bible claims exclusive authority in revealing God’s plan of redemption through Jesus Christ.
Jesus answered, “I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.” -
John 14:6 NIV
Science and Scripture can coexist, so long as we respect the boundaries and purposes of each.
Conclusion: Faith and Reason Together

The Bible does not fundamentally contradict science when both are properly understood. Scientific discoveries can complement and expand our wonder at God’s creation, while Scripture remains the foundation for understanding God’s character and His redemptive plan. Christians are encouraged to embrace both faith and reason, holding Scripture as the ultimate authority while appreciating the valuable insights gained through scientific inquiry.
